events.factual_description: Stephen Philip Harvey's official event listing presents the Stephen Philip Harvey Octet at Blues Alley in Washington, DC, on Sunday, November 1, 2026, with ticket links for 17:30 and 20:00 sets. The program is Mythos, a new original suite commissioned through Chamber Music America's 2025 New Jazz Works program. Harvey describes the suite as drawing on mythology from the African continent, mythology carried through the African diaspora, and U.S. folktales that evolved from that past. Chamber Music America's official 2025 grantee announcement independently confirms Stephen Philip Harvey Octet as a New Jazz Works recipient, identifies Harvey as leader/composer, and specifies an eight-piece instrumentation of alto saxophone, tenor saxophone, trumpet, trombone, guitar, piano, bass, and drums. Harvey's current calendar also lists Mythos commission-premiere performances in Pittsburgh on October 29 and Cleveland on October 30 before the Washington date, so the Blues Alley performance is part of a three-city premiere sequence rather than a unique world-premiere claim.

en.why_it_matters: This is not a routine SPH8 club date. Mythos is the public performance phase of Harvey's 2025 Chamber Music America New Jazz Works commission, written for an octet around stories that move from African mythology through the diaspora into U.S. folklore. The ensemble scale matters: two saxophones, brass, guitar, piano, bass and drums give the new suite enough room for layered writing without losing the reaction time of a working jazz group.
en.trip_verdict: If November 1 is open, Blues Alley is the clean DMV chance to hear Mythos right at the beginning of its public life. I would take advantage of the local date rather than move a harder-to-replace night around for it, especially because Washington follows two other commission-premiere stops that same week.

es.why_it_matters: Esta no es una fecha rutinaria de SPH8. Mythos es la salida al escenario de la comisión New Jazz Works 2025 de Chamber Music America: una suite para octeto construida alrededor de relatos que van de la mitología africana a la diáspora y de ahí al folclor de Estados Unidos. La escala del ensamble importa: dos saxofones, metales, guitarra, piano, bajo y batería permiten una escritura con capas sin perder la capacidad de reacción de un grupo de jazz en vivo.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 1 de noviembre está libre, Blues Alley es la oportunidad limpia en el DMV para escuchar Mythos al comienzo de su vida pública. Aprovecharía que está aquí sin mover una noche más difícil de reemplazar, sobre todo porque Washington llega después de otras dos presentaciones de estreno de la comisión esa misma semana.
